rawFindings.title: Incorrect handling of Windows absolute path with forward slashes in isAbsolute()
rawFindings.explanation: The original code considered paths like 'C:/' as absolute Windows device paths. The change removes support for forward slashes ('/') at path[2], only allowing backslashes ('\\'). This breaks detection of valid Windows absolute paths using forward slashes, e.g., 'c:/'.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore check for forward slash '/' in addition to '\\' at path[2]: if (':' === path[1] && ('\\' === path[2] || '/' === path[2])) return true;

rawFindings.title: Incorrect absolute path detection for Windows paths with forward slashes
rawFindings.explanation: The changed line removed support for recognizing Windows absolute paths that use a forward slash after the drive letter (e.g., 'C:/path'). This breaks absolute path detection for such Windows paths, which are valid and common.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore support for recognizing both backslash and forward slash after drive letter in Windows absolute path check, e.g. revert line 70 to: if (':' === path[1] && ('\\' === path[2] || '/' === path[2])) return true;

rawFindings.title: Incorrect Windows absolute path detection for forward slashes
rawFindings.explanation: The check for Windows device absolute path incorrectly requires a backslash at path[2], excluding valid paths with a forward slash (e.g., 'c:/'). The line changed from allowing both '\' and '/' at path[2] to only '\', reducing correct detection of absolute paths on Windows.
rawFindings.suggestion: Modify the condition to allow both backslash and forward slash at path[2], e.g. `if (':' === path[1] && ('\' === path[2] || '/' === path[2])) return true;` to properly detect Windows absolute paths with either separator.
